# 05 — Fix double %w error wrap in Telegram adapter

**What to build:** The Telegram adapter's S3 media download error uses `fmt.Errorf("%w: ... %w", ErrTelegramMediaRetryable, err)` — two `%w` verbs in a single wrap. The architecture doc mandates "one wrap per layer". While Go 1.20+ supports multi-`%w` via `Unwrap() []error`, single `errors.Unwrap()` returns `nil` for these, which is fragile and semantically ambiguous. Restructure to wrap only the sentinel error with `%w` and format the inner S3 error with `%v`, or use a custom error type that properly chains both.

**Blocked by:** None — can start immediately.

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] The `fmt.Errorf` in the Telegram adapter's S3 download path uses a single `%w` for `ErrTelegramMediaRetryable`
- [ ] The inner S3 error detail is still included in the error message (via `%v` or nested wrap)
- [ ] `errors.Is(err, ErrTelegramMediaRetryable)` still works correctly
- [ ] Update `telegram_challenge_test.go` to reflect the new wrapping structure (remove assertion on `errors.Is(err, s3Err)` if no longer applicable, or adjust)
- [ ] `telegram_test.go` S3 media download failure test continues to pass
title: Fix double %w error wrap in Telegram adapter

# 01 — Fix circuit breaker half-open state machine

**What to build:** The circuit breaker in `internal/platform/breaker` must correctly reset `consecutiveFailures` when transitioning from open → half-open. Currently, `RecordFailure` in half-open resets `openUntil` but does NOT reset `consecutiveFailures`, so the counter grows unboundedly across open→half-open→open cycles even though each cycle only had one actual probe failure. After this fix, the state machine matches the architecture doc: closed → open (at threshold) → half-open (after timeout) → one probe allowed → success closes, failure re-opens with a fresh failure count.

**Blocked by:** None — can start immediately.

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] `RecordFailure` resets `consecutiveFailures` appropriately when transitioning back to open from half-open (only 1 failure caused the re-open, counter reflects that)
- [ ] `RecordSuccess` in half-open correctly transitions to closed with zeroed counters (already works, verify)
- [ ] New test case in `breaker_test.go`: multi-cycle accumulation — run through 3+ open→half-open→open cycles and assert `consecutiveFailures` doesn't grow unboundedly
- [ ] All existing tests in `breaker_test.go` continue to pass
title: Fix circuit breaker half-open state machine

## What to build

Per `docs/SPEC-v1.8-BROADCASTER-GATEWAY.md` (US15): *"As a system operator, I want campaign execution logs to record every recipient dispatch state and trace ID in the `audit_logs` table, so that complete auditability and LGPD compliance are guaranteed."*

The audit batch writer (`internal/platform/audit/batch.go`) was recently improved with retry logic, partition management, and expvar counters — but the campaign worker does not call it. Each campaign dispatch state transition (enqueued → sent → delivered / failed) should produce an audit event.

- `workspace_id` from the campaign
- `trace_id` from the dispatch

- `payload` containing recipient ID, campaign ID, and error reason (if failed)

- [ ] Event types follow the pattern `campaign.dispatch.<status>` (sent, delivered, failed)

## What to build

The webhook dispatcher (`internal/webhook/dispatcher.go`) does not generate or attach the `X-PerGo-Signature` header on outbound webhook deliveries. Per the spec in `docs/SPEC-v1.8-BROADCASTER-GATEWAY.md` (US12, US13) and `docs/WEBHOOK_SIGNATURES.md`:

1. **Signature generation**: Before dispatching an outbound webhook POST, compute `HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + payload_bytes)` and attach header `X-PerGo-Signature: t=<unix_timestamp>,v1=<hex_digest>`.

2. **Per-workspace secret storage**: Add a `webhook_secret` column (or a dedicated table) so each workspace can configure its own HMAC signing key. Provide a REST endpoint or admin UI control to set/rotate this secret.

3. **Replay protection**: The timestamp component enables consumers to reject payloads older than 5 minutes (documented in `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURES.md`).

The crypto imports (`crypto/hmac`, `crypto/sha256`) are already present in `dispatcher.go` but unused for outbound signing — they are only used for inbound WABA verification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Outbound webhook POST requests include `X-PerGo-Signature` header in the format `t=<timestamp>,v1=<hmac_hex>`
- [ ] HMAC is computed as `SHA256(workspace_secret, "<timestamp>.<payload_bytes>")`
- [ ] A migration adds webhook secret storage per workspace
- [ ] An API endpoint or admin handler allows setting/rotating the webhook secret
- [ ] When no secret is configured for a workspace, the signature header is omitted (not an error)
- [ ] Unit tests verify correct signature generation and the header format
- [ ] Integration test verifies a delivered webhook carries a valid signature verifiable by the example code in `docs/WEBHOOK_SIGNATURES.md`

## Blocked by

- #40 — fix: implement half-open state in circuit breaker (the dispatcher uses the breaker and should be stable before adding signature logic)
title: feat: implement outbound webhook HMAC-SHA256 signature (X-PerGo-Signature)

## What to build

Several handlers violate the documented coding standards. This ticket addresses three related issues from the code review:

**1. Telegram error wrapping (docs/architecture/05-resilience-error-handling.md)**
In `internal/channel/telegram/telegram.go`, the S3 download error is wrapped with `%v` instead of `%w`:
`fmt.Errorf("%w: telegram media download from S3 failed: %v", ErrTelegramMediaRetryable, err)` — the inner `err` is not unwrappable. Fix to use `%w` for both errors or restructure to wrap the inner error properly.

**2. Fat CSV export handler (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md: keep handlers thin)**
`ExportContactsCSV` in `internal/api/handler/admin/tag.go` directly iterates contacts, queries tag repos per-contact in a loop, and assembles CSV inline. Extract this into a service function (e.g., in a contacts service or the tag repository layer) that the handler calls.

**3. Fat idempotency handler (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md: keep handlers thin)**
`Create` in `internal/api/handler/message.go` handles SHA-256 hashing, idempotency check-and-store, and ledger recording inline. Extract idempotency checking into a middleware or a service method the handler calls.

**4. Inline redirect handler in main.go**
The `adminGroup.GET("/tags", ...)` closure in `cmd/pergo/main.go` parses cookies, queries workspace repo, and issues redirects — this belongs on `TagAdminHandler` as a method, not as a closure in the composition root.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Telegram S3 error uses `%w` for both wrapped errors (inner error is unwrappable via `errors.Is`/`errors.As`)
- [ ] `ExportContactsCSV` handler delegates CSV assembly to a service/repository method
- [ ] Message `Create` handler delegates idempotency check to a separate function or middleware
- [ ] Inline `/tags` redirect closure in `main.go` is replaced by a `TagAdminHandler` method
- [ ] All existing tests still pass

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
title: refactor: fix error wrapping and extract business logic from fat handlers

body:
## What to build

The circuit breaker in `internal/platform/breaker/breaker.go` is missing the **half-open** state. Per `docs/architecture/05-resilience-error-handling.md`, the breaker must implement 3 states:

- **closed** → call fn; on error, failures++; at threshold → open
- **open** → return `ErrCircuitOpen` immediately for `openTime`
- **half-open** → allow one probe; success → closed, failure → open

Currently, when `resetTimeout` expires, `Allow()` resets `consecutiveFailures` to 0 and returns nil — transitioning directly from open → closed, skipping half-open entirely. A single failure after timeout should immediately re-trip the breaker, not require `maxFailures` consecutive failures again.

Add a `state` field (closed/open/halfOpen) to `EndpointBreaker`. When `openUntil` expires in `Allow()`, transition to halfOpen instead of closed. In halfOpen, allow exactly one request through. `RecordSuccess` from halfOpen → closed. `RecordFailure` from halfOpen → open (reset the timer).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `EndpointBreaker` tracks an explicit state (closed, open, halfOpen)
- [ ] After `resetTimeout` expires, the breaker enters halfOpen (not closed)
- [ ] In halfOpen, exactly one call is allowed through
- [ ] A success in halfOpen transitions to closed
- [ ] A failure in halfOpen transitions back to open with a fresh `resetTimeout`
- [ ] Tests cover all 6 state transitions: closed→open, open→halfOpen, halfOpen→closed, halfOpen→open, closed stays closed on success, open stays open before timeout
- [ ] Implementation remains ≤80 LoC as per architecture doc guidance

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
title: fix: implement half-open state in circuit breaker
